heritageSites.name: Taj Mahal
heritageSites.historicalBackground: Commissioned in 1631 by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan to house the tomb of his favourite wife, Mumtaz Mahal. Built over 22 years by more than 20,000 artisans.
heritageSites.culturalSignificance: Universally admired masterpiece of world heritage, representing the pinnacle of Mughal artistic achievement and timeless devotion.
heritageSites.architecturalDetails: Constructed from translucent white Makrana marble featuring symmetrical charbagh gardens, pietra dura floral inlays with semi-precious stones, and four freestanding minarets.

guidelines: Electric vehicles operate from Shilpgram parking.
Strictly zero plastic permitted inside the monument.

heritageSites.name: Group of Monuments at Hampi
heritageSites.historicalBackground: Capital of the illustrious Vijayanagara Empire in the 14th century. Described by Portuguese and Persian travellers as one of the largest and most prosperous metropolises in the world.
heritageSites.culturalSignificance: Spectacular testimony to Dravidian art and architecture, immortalizing South India’s golden age of sculpture, astronomy, and trade.
heritageSites.architecturalDetails: Over 1,600 surviving monuments set in dramatic boulder-strewn terrain, featuring the famed Stone Chariot, musical pillars of Vittala Temple, and Virupaksha shrine.

guidelines: Rent eco-friendly bicycles or hire authorized ASI guides.

heritageSites.name: Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram
heritageSites.historicalBackground: Port city of the 7th-century Pallava dynasty, serving as a maritime trading hub connecting ancient India to Southeast Asia.
heritageSites.culturalSignificance: Pioneered monolithic rock-cut cave temples and freestanding monolithic rathas that set the foundation for Dravidian temple design.
heritageSites.architecturalDetails: Features the dramatic Shore Temple braving the Bay of Bengal surf, Pancha Rathas carved out of single granite boulders, and the colossal bas-relief Descent of the Ganges.

heritageSites.name: Mysore Palace (Amba Vilas)
heritageSites.historicalBackground: Seat of the Wadiyar dynasty who ruled the Kingdom of Mysore from 1399 to 1950. Designed by British architect Henry Irwin and completed in 1912.
heritageSites.culturalSignificance: Centerpiece of the celebrated 10-day Mysuru Dasara festival, visited by millions of domestic and international cultural travellers annually.
heritageSites.architecturalDetails: Indo-Saracenic grandeur blending Hindu, Mughal, Rajput, and Gothic styles with marble domes, stained glass ceilings, teakwood carvings, and 97,000 illumination bulbs.

heritageSites.name: City Palace, Jaipur
heritageSites.historicalBackground: Established in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II alongside the founding of the planned city of Jaipur.
heritageSites.culturalSignificance: Living museum and continuing residence of the Jaipur royal family, housing treasured textiles, manuscripts, armouries, and royal carriages.
heritageSites.architecturalDetails: Combines Rajput, Mughal, and European architecture with courtyards, Pritam Niwas Chowk peacock gate, Chandra Mahal, and Mubarak Mahal.

guidelines: Special museum passes available for the private royal quarters.

heritageSites.name: Konark Sun Temple
heritageSites.historicalBackground: Built in the 13th century by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty in honour of Surya, the Sun God.
heritageSites.culturalSignificance: Pinnacle of Kalinga architecture, also known as the Black Pagoda by ancient European mariners navigating the Bay of Bengal.
heritageSites.architecturalDetails: Conceived as a colossal chariot of the Sun God, with 24 carved stone wheels that function as accurate sundials, drawn by seven galloping stone horses.

guidelines: Evening light and sound show available in English and Odia.

heritageSites.name: Qutub Minar & Complex
heritageSites.historicalBackground: Construction begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1199 and completed by Iltutmish and Firoz Shah Tughlaq. Represents the beginning of Delhi Sultanate rule.
heritageSites.culturalSignificance: Tallest brick minaret in the world at 72.5 metres, surrounded by historical architectural remnants spanning centuries.
heritageSites.architecturalDetails: Red sandstone fluted shaft with ornate geometric carving, Quranic calligraphic bands, and the mysterious 1,600-year-old rust-resistant Gupta Iron Pillar.

guidelines: Accessible via Delhi Metro Yellow Line (Qutub Minar Station).

heritageSites.name: Ajanta Caves
heritageSites.historicalBackground: Rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments carved in two phases between the 2nd century BCE and 5th century CE under the Satavahana and Vakataka dynasties.
heritageSites.culturalSignificance: Universally acclaimed masterpieces of ancient Buddhist religious art, containing expressive fresco paintings depicting Jataka tales.
heritageSites.architecturalDetails: 30 horseshoe-shaped volcanic basalt cliff caves overlooking the Waghur river ravine, comprising prayer halls (chaityas) and monasteries (viharas).

guidelines: Eco-friendly shuttle buses convey visitors from T-Junction parking area to caves.
